forbidden_claims: The source pack observed successful authenticated or private Galaxy reads.
The captured 403 authentication boundaries prove authenticated response semantics.
reason: The capture supplied no credentials. It preserves anonymous public responses and selected 403 boundaries, but no successful authenticated or private read was provider-executed.

forbidden_claims: Any of the 24 selected write shapes was executed against usegalaxy.org.
Local shadow transitions, read-after-write checks, reset checks, or projection self-tests are provider-executed Galaxy evidence.
reason: All 34 provider capture records are GET requests. The 24 write shapes are official-source contract candidates only; current local-shadow behavior and self-tests are not provider execution evidence.

forbidden_claims: The source pack validates arbitrary Galaxy workflows or the full Galaxy API.
The captured IWC AMR workflow establishes semantics for unrelated workflow templates.
reason: The selected construction scope centers on a bounded IWC AMR workflow and selected operation families. Administration, adjacent services, and unrelated workflow templates remain outside the evidence.

forbidden_claims: Galaxy Main was deployed from commit a7f8b9a0d3169d5344e291826804bf13b369d4a1.
The pinned source snapshot proves the exact deployed usegalaxy.org source revision.
reason: Commit a7f8b9a0d3169d5344e291826804bf13b369d4a1 and its per-file hashes are exact pins for a contemporaneous source snapshot, but the public capture exposes no deployed-commit proof.

forbidden_claims: The capture establishes Galaxy Main latency, throughput, availability, or an SLA.
The recorded request interval predicts future provider timing or availability.
reason: The dated capture records request and completion timestamps for one collection run only. It contains no controlled latency measurements, availability study, throughput evidence, or service-level commitment.

forbidden_claims: The source pack captures or replays arbitrary binary Galaxy dataset responses.
UTF-8 text capture proves byte fidelity for binary data.
reason: The provider recipe accepts JSON and bounded UTF-8 text. It did not capture a binary response representation, so binary dataset bodies and binary content negotiation are unsupported.

forbidden_claims: The preserved capture contains the raw provider response bytes.
Parsed JSON or decoded UTF-8 bodies can always reconstruct byte-identical provider responses.
The preserved capture-file SHA-256 is a provider response-body digest.
reason: The capture file itself is preserved byte-for-byte, and each response records its original byte count and SHA-256. The response payload is retained only as parsed JSON or decoded UTF-8 text, not as raw HTTP body bytes, so general byte-identical response replay is not established.
